dialogue.speaker: Pip
dialogue.text: Mr. Pumblechook’s boy, ma’am. Come—to play.

dialogue.speaker: Miss Havisham
dialogue.text: Come nearer; let me look at you. Come close.

dialogue.speaker: Miss Havisham
dialogue.text: Look at me. You are not afraid of a woman who has never seen the sun since you were born?

dialogue.speaker: Miss Havisham
dialogue.text: Do you know what I touch here?

dialogue.speaker: Miss Havisham
dialogue.text: I am tired. I want diversion, and I have done with men and women. Play.

dialogue.speaker: Miss Havisham
dialogue.text: I sometimes have sick fancies, and I have a sick fancy that I want to see some play. There, there! play, play, play!

dialogue.speaker: Pip
dialogue.text: No, ma’am, I am very sorry for you, and very sorry I can’t play just now. If you complain of me I shall get into trouble with my sister, so I would do it if I could; but it’s so new here, and so strange, and so fine,—and melancholy—.

dialogue.speaker: Miss Havisham
dialogue.text: So new to him, so old to me; so strange to him, so familiar to me; so melancholy to both of us! Call Estella.

dialogue.speaker: Miss Havisham
dialogue.text: You can do that. Call Estella. At the door.

Miss Havisham.name: Miss Havisham
Miss Havisham.personality: eccentric, melancholic, manipulative, theatrical, emotionally fragile
Miss Havisham.speech_style: formal, dramatic, indirect, prone to rambling and repetition
Miss Havisham.description: An elderly woman living in a decaying mansion, frozen in time after being jilted at the altar. She is surrounded by relics of her past and exhibits a strange, unsettling demeanor.

Pip.name: Pip
Pip.speech_style: deferential, verbose, hesitant, prone to lying and self-justification
Pip.description: A young boy, sent to entertain Miss Havisham. He is intimidated by her presence and struggles to navigate the strange and unsettling environment.

context: Pip, a young boy, is brought to Miss Havisham's decaying mansion to entertain her. The scene establishes the unsettling atmosphere of the house and the peculiar dynamic between the two characters, highlighting Miss Havisham's grief and Pip's discomfort.
